status: draft derived from the current bank structure + stated assumptions; needs product-owner sign-off
assumptions: Exam structure stays 4 Listening parts x 10 questions + 3 Reading parts x 13 questions = 79 MCQ (taken from config/blueprint.json parts_per_test/items_per_part).
Level used for blueprint checks is the recorded level.cefr; the heuristic CEFR recommendations (reports/cefr_reassessment.csv) are NOT used because they are unvalidated.
Primary sub-skill comes from config/question_meta_v2.json (generated by qa/stage5_taxonomy.py).
Hard constraints are never relaxed: if no valid exam is found within max_attempts the assembler raises BlueprintError.

assembly.attempt_seed_policy: attempt k draws with random.Random(f'{seed}:{k}'); k=0 is the legacy draw

forbidden_pairs_note: Populate from reports/duplicate_candidates.csv (kind=source or item with similarity>=0.9). The current bank has no such pairs.

rationale.levels: Every CEFR level must appear (min 3 questions each, i.e. >=3.8%) and none may dominate (max 35%). Counts need not be equal or bell-shaped. 3 questions is a floor for presence, NOT enough for a reliable estimate at A1 or C2 (see docs/remaining_risks.md).
rationale.profiles: Each skill must contain a foundation, an intermediate and an advanced part so weak and strong learners both meet answerable and separating items.
rationale.topics: No topic twice: 7 parts, 20+ available topics.

rationale.levels: Assumption: the product asks for a strictly level-specific assessment (the bank was built level-pure). Adjacent-level items are NOT allowed. If the product wants a target-level-dominant exam with limited adjacent items, relax level_counts and add adjacent-level parts to the bank first.
rationale.subskills: A1/A2 listening items in the bank are all detail retrieval, so only 1 distinct sub-skill can be required there (bank limitation, not a design choice).
